simple.meaning: חֶמֶד (chemed) is a Hebrew word meaning “delight.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חֶמֶד (H2531) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Isaiah 27:2, with occurrences in Isaiah, Ezekiel, Amos.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֶמֶד (H2531) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חֶמֶד (H2531) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חֶמֶד (chemed) / H2531 is traced through Isaiah 27:2, Isaiah 32:12, Ezekiel 23:6, Ezekiel 23:12 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H2531. chemed חֶ֫מֶד noun [masculine] desire, delight — absolute ׳ח Amos 5:11 + 4 t.; only after a construct; ׳כַּרְמֵיחֿ נְטַעְתֶּם 5:11 vineyards of desire (i.e. delightful vineyards) have ye planted ; so read also Isa 27:2 (for חֶמֶר כֶּרֶם ᵑ0 ) Manuscripts HCT ᵐ5 van d. H Lo Hi Ew De Di Che Du; so of fields ח ׳שְׁדֵי 32:12 ; elsewhere of young men ח ׳בַּחוּרֵי Ezek 23:6 , 12 , 23 desirable young men = fine, attractive, young men.
